BatchDefinition.description: Several VMs from one base configuration.

base_vm.description: The configuration every instance starts from: inline, a path to a config file, or the name of an existing VM to copy.

instances.description: One entry per VM, each overriding part of the base.

name.description: A name for the batch itself.

acpi.description: Enable ACPI support (required by most modern OSes).

boot1.description: The first boot slot, kept in step with ``order``. Set ``order`` instead; these exist because every provider addresses slots individually.

ioapic.description: Enable I/O APIC (required for more than one CPU or for Windows).

order.description: Ordered list of boot devices; valid values are ``"disk"``, ``"dvd"``, ``"floppy"``, ``"network"``, ``"none"``.

execution_cap.description: Maximum percentage of host CPU time the VM may use (1–100).

hotplug.description: Allow CPUs to be added/removed while the VM is running.

model.description: The CPU model the guest sees: ``host`` to pass the host's CPU through, ``host-model`` for the closest migratable description, or a named model such as ``Skylake-Client``. None leaves it to the provider. VirtualBox has no such setting and reports it (A-10).

nested_virt.description: Enable nested virtualisation (required for running KVM inside VirtualBox).

pae.description: Enable Physical Address Extension for 32-bit OSes.

sockets.description: Sockets to present, or None to let the provider decide.

ballooning.description: Enable dynamic memory ballooning (guest must support it).

page_fusion.description: Enable kernel same-page merging to reduce physical RAM usage.

adapter_name.description: Physical or virtual interface name used for BRIDGED / HOSTONLY modes.

mac_address.description: Custom MAC address; ``None`` lets VirtualBox assign one automatically.

model.description: The network chipset the guest sees. Was ``adapter_type``, which held VirtualBox's own id (``"82540EM"``) in the neutral model (A-10).

network_type.description: Connection mode (NAT, BRIDGED, HOSTONLY, INTERNAL, NATNETWORK).

port_forwards.description: Host ports forwarded into the guest. Only meaningful on a NAT adapter -- every other mode reaches the guest directly -- and not every provider can express them (E-10).

promiscuous_mode.description: Allow the adapter to receive packets not addressed to it.

provider_options.description: Native details with no neutral equivalent, by provider name. This is what keeps a same-provider round trip exact where the neutral vocabulary is deliberately coarser: VirtualBox has three Intel PRO/1000 variants that are all ``e1000`` to the model, and re-creating the VM should give the guest back the same card, not the family's default (A-10).

guest_ip.description: Which guest address to send to. Empty means the address the guest's DHCP gave it, which is what a NAT adapter normally wants.

guest_port.description: The port inside the guest. Required.

host_ip.description: Which host address to listen on. Empty means all of them, which is what every provider means by leaving it out -- and a reason to set it: ``127.0.0.1`` keeps a lab's forwarded ports off the network.

host_port.description: The port on this machine. Required; there is no default worth guessing.

name.description: What the rule is called. VirtualBox needs one and requires it to be unique; the others have no such concept, so vmctl fills one in rather than making every config carry a field only one provider reads.

bootable.description: Whether the firmware may boot from this controller.

bus.description: The bus this controller implements. Was ``controller_type``, which was documented as a chipset and valued as a bus.

id.description: Stable logical key, e.g. ``"sata0"``. What devices reference, and what stays the same when the same VM is expressed on another hypervisor.

model.description: Neutral model name, when the bus offers a choice. The chipset a provider uses to implement it is that provider's business, resolved through its tables.

native_name.description: What the provider calls it (``"SATA Controller"``). Kept so a same-provider round trip is faithful; meaningless anywhere else, which is why it is separate from ``id``.

port_count.description: How many ports to give it, or None for the provider's own default -- which is the only safe answer, since a bus may accept exactly one number (IDE takes 2, USB takes 8) and it differs per provider.

bootable.description: Mark this device as a boot device.

bus.description: The interface it hangs off. Was ``controller`` -- which named a *bus* while ``controller_name`` named a *controller*, one word doing two jobs (M-02).

controller.description: Which controller to attach to: a :attr:`StorageController.id`, or a provider's own name for one, or None to take whichever controller serves ``bus``. Was ``controller_name``.

discard.description: Pass the guest's TRIM/UNMAP through to the host, so freeing space in the guest frees it on the host.

disk_path.description: Where the image is on the source host. Never exported: it describes a host, not the VM.

format.description: Image format, or None for whichever format the provider creates natively. None is what keeps a config portable: it is the difference between "a disk" and "a VirtualBox disk" (M-04).

hotpluggable.description: Let the guest detach the device while it is running.

kind.description: What the guest sees: a disk, a CD-ROM or a floppy drive. Was ``type``.

name.description: Identifier for this device within the VM (e.g. ``"system"``).

nonrotational.description: Present the disk to the guest as solid-state. Was ``type: ssd`` (M-01).

provider_options.description: Settings only one hypervisor has, carried verbatim. vmctl does not interpret them; they exist so that a native detail can survive a round trip on its own provider instead of being dropped, without every such detail having to become a neutral field first.

size_mb.description: Capacity in megabytes. None on a removable drive, which has none; a disk that does not say gets :data:`DEFAULT_DISK_MB`.

slot.description: Port on the controller (0-based), or None to be assigned. Was ``port``.

source.description: An existing medium to attach instead of creating one -- an ISO for an optical drive, or an image that already exists, which is how a migration attaches the converted copy of a disk.

unit.description: Device on that slot (0 or 1 on IDE), or None to be assigned. Was ``device``.

arch.description: The architecture the guest's virtual CPU presents. VirtualBox has no such setting -- a VM runs the host's -- while libvirt requires one in every domain (A-10).

audio_enabled.description: Whether the guest gets a sound device.

boot.description: What the VM tries to boot from, in order, plus the firmware-adjacent switches that belong with it.

clipboard_mode.description: Clipboard sharing with the host: ``disabled``, ``hosttoguest``, ``guesttohost`` or ``bidirectional``. Needs guest additions, and not every provider has it.

cpu.description: The virtual CPU: how many, and how they are arranged.

description.description: A note about what this VM is for. Kept where the provider has somewhere to put it -- libvirt has a description field, VirtualBox does not.

draganddrop.description: Drag and drop between host and guest, with the same values as :attr:`clipboard_mode`.

firmware.description: Firmware: BIOS or EFI, secure boot, TPM.

guest_os.description: Which OS the guest runs, as a neutral id from :mod:`vmctl.core.oscatalog` (``ubuntu22.04``, ``win11``) -- or a provider's own string, which passes through untranslated. Was ``ostype``, whose default was the VirtualBox id ``Ubuntu_64``: the last vendor spelling left in the canonical model (A-05).

machine.description: The machine type (chipset) to emulate, such as ``q35`` or ``pc``. None means the provider's own default, which is the portable answer: the set on offer depends on the QEMU build, and VirtualBox has no choice at all.

memory.description: Memory, and video memory where the provider has such a setting.

metadata.description: Anything vmctl should carry but not act on. Two uses: a user's own annotations, and a provider's native identifiers -- a libvirt domain's UUID lives here, which is what lets ``edit`` redefine that domain rather than create a second one.

name.description: What the VM is called. It identifies the VM to the hypervisor and ends up in file paths, so the providers' declarations say what a name may contain.

networks.description: The network adapters, in the order the provider numbers them.

rtc_utc.description: Whether the guest's hardware clock reads UTC. Right for everything except a Windows guest, which expects local time.

schema_version.description: Which version of the configuration format this came from. A file that does not say is taken to be the current one, which is what it almost always is -- and the 1.1.x names are accepted whatever this says, so an old file needs no edit (E-14).

storage.description: Every device on a bus -- disks, optical drives, floppies -- in one list, because that is what they are. Was ``disks:``, which the list never only held (M-02).

storage_controllers.description: The controllers the devices hang off. Optional: a provider synthesises whatever a device's bus needs, so a hand-written config does not have to declare them (F-01). Declaring them is how a specific chipset or port count is asked for.

usb_enabled.description: Whether the guest gets a USB controller.

description: A virtual machine, or a batch that creates several from one base -- in terms no hypervisor owns. Generated from vmctl's own model, so it cannot describe a file vmctl would reject, and it accepts the 1.1.x field names.
title: vmctl configuration
